summary.intent: Execute all plans in GSD phase 68.1 (web client runtime integration) using wave-based parallel subagent execution, with the orchestrator staying lean (discover plans, group into dependency waves, spawn subagents, gate, merge, track).
summary.outcome: 13 of 14 plans completed and merged across 4 waves with passing build/test gates; the final exit-gate plan (68.1-13) ran the full 208-spec web-e2e suite, surfaced 17 failures, and a headed re-run of full-workflow.spec.ts confirmed a real bug (nested folder creation fails silently) that a triage subagent was dispatched to fix, so the phase is not yet fully closed.

repo: Wave dependency grouping in cipher-box's execute-phase workflow: plans touching the same file (e.g. packages/sdk/src/client.ts) must be forced sequential on the main tree even within a 'wave', while file-disjoint plans run in parallel worktrees.

resolveFileMetadata needed its signature changed from a bare fileIpnsName string to the full SealedChildRef because readKeySealed/generation (needed to derive the file's own readKey via unsealChildReadKey) only exist on the parent's SealedChildRef.

Web app has no SdkContext bridge, so file preview/download (68.1-04) had to be implemented against web-native primitives (ipns.service.ts's resolveIpnsRecord, ctx-free fetchFromIpfs) rather than sdk-core's ctx-based helpers — this also preserves the ROT-07 anti-rollback floor missing from sdk-core's raw resolveIpnsRecord.

Live /shares and /shares/invites REST API grants an entire subtree via a single ECIES wrap of the root readKey — there is no per-child-key server field, confirming collectChildKeys (SHARE-WRITE-KEY related) has no live caller even though it's implemented correctly per spec (matches existing memory project-cipherbox-collect-child-keys.md).

sdk-core's issueReadGrant/claimInvite (grant.ts) produce base64 payloads but live DTOs are hex-only, so web code calls wrapKey/unwrapKey directly with hex encoding instead of routing through sdk-core's grant primitives.

Writable share/invite creation is blocked by design: deriving a shared item's writeKey needs the parent folder's writeKey, which currently lives only inside CipherBoxClient's private FolderState (from 68.1-01) and isn't threaded to any web UI layer — flagged as the 'SHARE-WRITE-KEY web-wiring gap' needing a dedicated cross-cutting gap-closure plan.
sdk-core's updateFileMetadata never actually zeroed fileIpnsPrivateKey despite call-site doc comments claiming it did (latent bug T-47-01), fixed during 68.1-12.

replaceFile/restoreFileVersion/deleteFileVersion (from 68.1-09) require the caller to pre-resolve fileIpnsPrivateKey, but NODE-03's frozen SealedChildRef schema gives the web layer no independent way to derive it — required adding a new public client.resolveFileIpnsPrivateKey method.
web-tier fetchShareKeys is still a deferred Phase-68 stub, causing shared move/update-fallback to fail closed until real share-key delivery is wired.

The cipherbox-mock-ipns-routing docker container had been unhealthy for 39 hours during the e2e run — a likely root cause for IPNS-heavy test failures (recovery, rotation, shared flows) independent of app code bugs.

Creating a folder nested inside another folder fails silently in the web UI (dialog closes, no error, child never appears) — root-level folder creation works via rootWriteKey (68.1-03) but subfolders take a different write-body/writeKey path (68.1-01/68.1-02, ensureFolderLoaded), and the bug lives around apps/web/src/hooks/useFolderMutations.ts.

code.finding: Suspected location of a bug where creating a subfolder inside another folder fails silently; confirmed by headed Playwright run of full-workflow.spec.ts aborting at 'Create documents folder inside workspace'.
New public method resolveFileIpnsPrivateKey added in 68.1-12 to let the web layer derive a file's IPNS private key without direct access to CipherBoxClient's private writeKey state.
updateFileMetadata now actually zeroes fileIpnsPrivateKey after use, fixing a latent bug where the doc comment claimed this but the code never did it.

workflow: GSD wave execution pattern: orchestrator spawns one subagent per plan per wave in isolated git worktrees, records worktree_metadata as each returns, merges all worktrees back only after the full wave completes, then runs post-merge build/test gates and drift checks before advancing.

Background agent task-notifications can be silently lost even when the underlying work (e.g. a long e2e suite) completes successfully — orchestrator had to manually probe process liveness and read raw log output to detect the suite had actually finished before resuming the executor.

When a subagent stalls mid-stream (no notification, no output) for an extended period, spot-check filesystem/git state directly rather than assuming a freeze, then resume the same agent via SendMessage with its full context so it can finish and self-verify.

Serial (describe.serial) Playwright specs abort at first failure, so a raw failed-test count can overstate coverage/health — most failures may just be downstream of one early setup failure rather than independent bugs.
User skepticism about a background e2e run was resolved by running the specific failing spec headed and screenshotting the failure, rather than relying solely on the earlier automated triage summary.

friction: Wave 1 agent (plan 68.1-01) stalled mid-stream after 119 tool calls (~23 min) with no completion signal, requiring the orchestrator to spot-check state and manually resume it via SendMessage.
Transient git index.lock encountered during Wave 3 tracking commit, requiring a retry.

Wave 5 exit-gate agent's completion signal for the 208-spec e2e suite was never delivered (lost wake-up); the agent's session was evicted after launching the suite in the background, leaving the orchestrator believing it was still running long after it had actually finished at 18:13.
No Playwright HTML report was available after the run, forcing the orchestrator to extract pass/fail/skip counts from raw stdout logs.
mock-ipns-routing docker container was unhealthy for 39 hours, a plausible confound for several IPNS-related e2e failures that complicates root-causing them as app bugs vs. infra issues.
open_items: SHARE-WRITE-KEY web-wiring gap (write-permission share/invite creation blocked by UI error) needs a dedicated cross-cutting gap-closure plan touching SDK client → useFolderNavigation → folder.store → FileBrowser.tsx → ShareDialog.tsx; also no backend 'upgrade permission' endpoint exists yet (would need revoke+recreate).
web-tier fetchShareKeys remains a deferred stub causing shared move/update-fallback to fail closed.

17/208 e2e failures need triage: some expected (writable-shares, shared-folder-move, invite-link/journey-share tied to known gaps above) and some needing real fixes (batch-download, recycle-bin, bin-restore, media-preview, streaming-playback, conflict-detection, move-restore, full-workflow, mfa-deny, recovery, rotation-durability, share-itemname-backfill).

Confirmed real bug: nested folder creation fails silently in the web UI, suspected around apps/web/src/hooks/useFolderMutations.ts, blocking downstream tests that depend on nested content — a continuation/triage agent was actively working this fix at transcript end.
mock-ipns-routing container unhealthy status (39h) should be investigated as a possible cause of IPNS-related e2e failures before concluding they're code bugs.
Phase 68.1 completion (gsd-verifier, phase.complete, PROJECT.md update) is still pending final triage results from plan 68.1-13.
